# CSPM benchmark coverage

<!-- Generated by `go run ./cmd/cspm-coverage` from internal/checks/benchmarks/*.yaml, internal/checks/frameworks/*.yaml and the check registry. Do not edit. -->

Vulngraph's CSPM mapped against public cloud benchmarks, control by control. Statuses are a maintainer-declared mapping: `covered` means the listed registry check(s) are judged to evaluate the control's condition; `partial` evaluates part of it; `missing` is evaluable from cloud APIs but has no check yet; `not_applicable` is outside what an API-driven scanner can see; `manual` needs human evidence. Tests check that every cited check exists for the benchmark's provider, and a scheduled job compares control IDs with the pinned upstream list (ADR 092); nothing checks that each check is equivalent to its control. Control IDs and paraphrased titles only — no benchmark text is reproduced.

"Checked against upstream" is when `go run ./cmd/benchmark-watch -update` last compared the matrix's control IDs with the public list it is pinned to (ADR 092).

## Requirement frameworks

NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 is built in. Add your own frameworks (HIPAA, FedRAMP, an internal standard) with `FRAMEWORKS_DIR`; the format and worked examples are in [`docs/frameworks`](frameworks/README.md). Requirement-level mappings live in `internal/checks/frameworks`. A requirement counts as mapped when at least one benchmark control it maps has a registry check; whether it passes is decided live from findings and inventory. "Partial source mapping" counts requirements where some source mappings (a Prowler check, an AWS related FSBP control) reach no graph control; those can never pass. "Can pass" counts requirements with no structural gap: every control they map is fully covered by a check and every source mapping reaches one. Every other requirement shows failing or unknown at best, except that a control for a provider you do not connect is out of scope and does not block a pass, however much of it is covered. Requirement IDs and short titles only; titles are paraphrased where the standard is copyrighted.

| Framework | Version | Requirements | Can pass | With ≥1 mapped check | Mapped to a control only | No mapping | Partial source mapping |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| NIST SP 800-53 | Rev. 5 | 222 | 138 (62%) | 216 | 0 | 6 | 74 |

## Kubernetes namespace exemptions

These Kubernetes checks skip fixed namespace lists, set in code and not configurable. Nothing is reported for a resource in an exempt namespace, so a benchmark control marked covered above is not graded there. Each check's description, shown on its findings, names its list.

| Applies to | Namespaces never evaluated | Why | Checks |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pod checks | `calico-system`, `cert-manager`, `datadog`, `falco`, `gke-system`, `gmp-public`, `gmp-system`, `istio-system`, `kube-node-lease`, `kube-public`, `kube-system`, `monitoring`, and any namespace labelled `pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce=privileged` | Node agents (CNI, CSI, metadata servers, monitoring and security agents) need privileged access and host namespaces there, and an operator who labels a namespace privileged has declared the same. Names match exactly, so an application namespace that happens to be called monitoring is skipped too. A privileged pod placed in one of these namespaces is not reported, so review them by other means (admission policy, runtime detection); k8s-namespace-no-pod-security-enforcement still reports a privileged label outside this list. | `k8s-container-added-capabilities`, `k8s-container-allow-privilege-escalation`, `k8s-container-host-port`, `k8s-container-net-raw`, `k8s-container-writable-root-fs`, `k8s-dangerous-capabilities`, `k8s-host-ipc-pod`, `k8s-host-network-pod`, `k8s-host-pid-pod`, `k8s-pod-apparmor-unconfined`, `k8s-pod-host-path-volume`, `k8s-pod-seccomp-unrestricted`, `k8s-pod-secret-in-env`, `k8s-privileged-container`, `k8s-windows-host-process` |
| Namespace admission and isolation | `calico-system`, `cert-manager`, `datadog`, `falco`, `gke-system`, `gmp-public`, `gmp-system`, `istio-system`, `kube-node-lease`, `kube-public`, `kube-system`, `monitoring` | The same platform namespaces as the pod checks. | `k8s-default-sa-automount`, `k8s-namespace-no-default-deny`, `k8s-namespace-no-pod-security-enforcement` |
| NetworkPolicy presence | `calico-system`, `cert-manager`, `gke-system`, `gmp-public`, `gmp-system`, `kube-node-lease`, `kube-public`, `kube-system`, `monitoring` | Their traffic policy is managed by the platform. | `k8s-namespace-no-network-policy` |
| Resource limits | `calico-system`, `cert-manager`, `gke-system`, `gmp-system`, `kube-system`, `monitoring` | Their resource profiles are managed by the platform. | `k8s-pod-no-resource-limits` |
| ConfigMap plaintext secrets | `calico-system`, `cert-manager`, `gke-system`, `gmp-public`, `gmp-system`, `istio-system`, `kube-node-lease`, `kube-public`, `kube-system`, `monitoring` | The collector does not record ConfigMaps there, so a plaintext secret in one is not reported: their ConfigMaps are the platform's. | `k8s-configmap-plaintext-secret` |

## AWS Foundational Security Best Practices 1.0.0

### Missing

**bedrock**

- `Bedrock.1` Bedrock data sources encrypted with a customer managed KMS key — No Bedrock knowledge-base collector: needs bedrock-agent:ListKnowledgeBases, ListDataSources and GetDataSource (serverSideEncryptionConfiguration.kmsKeyArn) per region. Not collected, so not graded.

**bedrock-agentcore**

- `BedrockAgentCore.7` AgentCore custom code interpreters use a private network — The AgentCore collector lists runtimes, gateways and custom browsers only; custom code interpreters (bedrock-agentcore-control:ListCodeInterpreters + GetCodeInterpreter networkConfiguration.networkMode, PUBLIC or SANDBOX fails) are not collected yet.

**sagemaker**

- `SageMaker.23` Inference experiments encrypt instance storage with a customer managed key — Inference experiments are not collected: needs sagemaker:ListInferenceExperiments + DescribeInferenceExperiment (KmsKey).
- `SageMaker.24` Inference experiments encrypt captured data with a customer managed key — Inference experiments are not collected: needs sagemaker:ListInferenceExperiments + DescribeInferenceExperiment (DataStorageConfig.KmsKey).

### Partial

**apigateway**

- `APIGateway.9` API Gateway V2 stages have access logging — Every v2 (HTTP and WebSocket) stage the control covers is graded: apigatewayv2:GetStages accessLogSettings.destinationArn as access_log_destination on api_gateway_stage ("" when off, absent when unread), one finding per stage. Partial, not covered, by choice: the same check also fires on REST stages, which CIS AWS 4.10 needs and APIGateway.9 does not cover, so mapping this row is broader than the control (an api_type=REST finding is CIS 4.10 evidence only). Splitting it would put two findings on every v2 stage.

**neptune**

- `Neptune.6` Neptune cluster snapshots encrypted at rest — Manual cluster snapshots are graded directly; an automated snapshot always has its cluster's encryption, so the cluster check reports it once. Not covered: automated backups retained after their cluster was deleted (rds:DescribeDBClusterAutomatedBackups is not collected).

**rds**

- `RDS.4` RDS snapshots encrypted at rest — Manual DB and cluster snapshots are graded directly. An automated snapshot always has its source's encryption, so an unencrypted one exists only for an unencrypted instance or cluster, which its source check reports (one finding per root cause). Not covered: automated backups retained after their source was deleted (rds:DescribeDBInstanceAutomatedBackups / DescribeDBClusterAutomatedBackups are not collected).


## CIS Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) Benchmark 1.8.0

### Missing

**acr**

- `5.1.3` Cluster gets read-only registry access — Needs the cluster's kubelet identity (identityProfile.kubeletidentity.objectId, in the managed-cluster response) joined to its role assignments on Microsoft.ContainerRegistry/registries scopes (AcrPull only, not AcrPush/Contributor/Owner); no registry collector exists and the identities collector does not resolve assignments per registry.

**aks-logging**

- `2.1.1` Turn on AKS control plane audit logs — Needs Microsoft.Insights/diagnosticSettings on each managed cluster (kube-audit / kube-audit-admin categories enabled). Clusters are collected (azure_aks_cluster); per-resource diagnostic settings belong to the Azure Monitor collector, which is not built yet.

**kubelet**

- `3.2.7` Kubelet event rate keeps adequate capture — The only testable condition (kube-bench: eventRecordQPS >= 0) is what kubelet configuration validation already enforces, so a check could never fire; graph does not ship one. eventRecordQPS is readable through the node posture reader if a threshold is ever published.

### Partial

**aks-network**

- `5.4.5` Load balancers terminate TLS with certificates — Only Kubernetes Ingress TLS is checked. Azure Load Balancer is layer 4 and terminates no TLS; Application Gateway listeners in front of the cluster (AGIC) are collected as azure_app_gateway but their listener protocols are not.

**defender**

- `5.1.1` Scan container images for vulnerabilities — Fires when the cluster's Defender security profile (securityProfile.defender.securityMonitoring) is off. The benchmark also accepts a third-party scanner, which nothing in ARM reports, so a cluster scanned by one still fires (Low, and the finding says so).

**general**

- `4.6.2` Apply security contexts to pods and containers — Running pods are evaluated for root/privilege escalation, privileged mode and three added capabilities; seccomp, AppArmor, read-only root filesystem and dropped capabilities are not recorded by the Kubernetes collector, and which context a workload needs is a judgement.

**identity**

- `5.2.1` Give workloads dedicated Azure identities — Fires when Microsoft Entra Workload ID is off on the cluster, so pods can only call Azure as the shared node identity or with a stored secret. With it on, whether each workload actually uses its own federated identity needs ServiceAccount annotations the Kubernetes collector does not record.

**network-policy**

- `4.4.2` Every namespace has a NetworkPolicy — Checks that some NetworkPolicy exists in each namespace (not what it allows; system namespaces including monitoring and cert-manager are exempt) and that the cluster runs an engine that enforces them.

**rbac**

- `4.1.1` Restrict cluster-admin role bindings to necessity — Every binding to cluster-admin is surfaced (cluster- and namespace-scoped); whether it is "required" is the reviewer's call, as in the benchmark audit. The cluster-scoped check also flags the built-in admin ClusterRole.
- `4.1.3` Avoid wildcards in Roles and ClusterRoles — hasWildcard ignores resources ["*"] paired with read-only verbs (get/list/watch); platform-managed roles are excluded by design.


## CIS Amazon Web Services Foundations Benchmark 7.0.0

### Partial

**iam**

- `2.21` Resource policies do not allow any principal — A policy that allows everyone (Principal "*", or an Allow with NotPrincipal) a sensitive action under no condition that restricts the caller, not taken back by an unconditional Deny that reaches everyone. A condition only on transport or client shape (aws:SecureTransport, aws:UserAgent) does not restrict the caller. Graded by the shared resource-policy evaluator for Lambda, KMS, SQS, SNS, ECR, Secrets Manager, EventBridge event buses, EFS file systems, Backup vaults and DynamoDB tables; S3 buckets by AWS's GetBucketPolicyStatus (aws-s3-public-read and aws-s3-public-write when the public part names its data actions, otherwise aws-s3-public-bucket, which also reports a public ACL and an incomplete Block Public Access, neither of them a resource policy); role trust policies by the trust evaluator (an Allow to Principal "*" with no Condition and no Deny confining it). OpenSearch access policies are read and graded the same way, but reported only for a public-endpoint domain (aws-opensearch-domain-public), so an open policy on a VPC domain is not. S3 Access Point policies are read only as AWS's GetAccessPointPolicyStatus verdict, which tiers FSBP S3.19. Not yet read: Glacier vault and API Gateway REST API policies.


## CIS Microsoft Azure Foundations Benchmark 6.0.0

### Missing

**databricks**

- `2.1.6` Databricks personal access tokens are restricted and expire — Needs the Databricks workspace REST API (workspace-conf maxTokenLifetimeDays, token permissions), which takes a workspace-admin Databricks token: Azure Reader on the workspace resource does not grant it, and the ARM resource does not expose these settings.
- `2.1.7` Databricks diagnostic log delivery configured — Needs Microsoft.Insights/diagnosticSettings on each Databricks workspace resource. Workspaces are now collected (azure_databricks_workspace); per-resource diagnostic settings belong to the Azure Monitor collector (6.1.4), which is not built yet.


## CIS Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (EKS) Benchmark 1.8.0

### Missing

**ecr**

- `5.1.2` Limit user access to ECR — Needs ECR write actions (ecr:Put*/BatchDelete*/*) analysed across IAM policy documents (existing iam collector `policies`) and repository policies (ecr:GetRepositoryPolicy, already read for public_access); no check evaluates it.

**eks-logging**

- `2.1.2` Audit logs are retained and managed — Needs logs:DescribeLogGroups for `/aws/eks/<cluster>/cluster` (existence, retentionInDays, KMS key); no CloudWatch Logs collector exists.

**iam**

- `5.2.1` Give workloads dedicated IAM identities — Needs correlation of pods with no IRSA/Pod Identity role (`exec_role` empty on `k8s_pod`) against the node instance role they then inherit (`iam_role_arn` on `ec2_instance`); Pod Identity associations need eks:ListPodIdentityAssociations.

**kubelet**

- `3.2.7` Kubelet event rate keeps adequate capture — CIS EKS marks it Automated, but its only testable condition (kube-bench: eventRecordQPS >= 0) is what kubelet configuration validation already enforces, so a check could never fire; graph does not ship one. eventRecordQPS is readable through the node posture reader if a threshold is ever published.

### Partial

**ecr**

- `5.1.1` Scan container images for vulnerabilities — Reads per-repository scan_on_push only; registry-level enhanced/continuous scanning (ecr:GetRegistryScanningConfiguration) is not read, so a registry with enhanced scanning can still fire, and third-party scanners are not recognised.

**elb**

- `5.4.5` Load balancers terminate TLS with certificates — Only Kubernetes Ingress TLS is checked; load-balancer listener protocols/certificates need elbv2:DescribeListeners (and elb:DescribeLoadBalancers listener descriptions), not collected.

## CIS Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) Benchmark 2.0.0

### Missing

**gke-logging**

- `5.7.2` auditd logging on COS nodes — Detectable only via the Google-provided auditd DaemonSet in the cluster (workload listing exists; no check, name-based heuristic).

**gke-storage**

- `5.9.1` CMEK-protected StorageClasses for persistent disks — Needs StorageClass objects (parameters `disk-encryption-kms-key`) from the K8s API; the K8s collector does not list StorageClasses.

### Partial

**artifact-registry**

- `5.1.2` Least-privilege IAM on Artifact Registry repos — Only public access is detected (repository IAM policies binding allUsers or allAuthenticatedUsers). Over-broad grants to named principals — writers who need only read, project-level artifactregistry roles held by many users — are not graded.

**gke-network**

- `5.6.6` Least-privilege firewall rules for nodes — A Manual recommendation in the benchmark. Internet-sourced ingress is flagged on each rule (whatever it targets, nodes included), but rules are not scoped to the node pools' network tags or service accounts, and whether internal sources are least-privilege for the workload is a design review no API answers.

**network-policy**

- `4.3.2` Default-deny NetworkPolicy per workload namespace — A namespace with no NetworkPolicy, or with policies but none that selects every pod and denies all ingress, fails. Egress default-deny is not evaluated, and system namespaces are exempt.

**pod-security**

- `4.6.3` Workloads run with hardened security contexts — Root, privilege escalation, privileged, capabilities (added, dangerous, NET_RAW), seccomp, explicit AppArmor Unconfined and readOnlyRootFilesystem are evaluated; runAsGroup and SELinux options are not.

**rbac**

- `4.1.6` Never grant admin through system:masters group — Flags RBAC bindings naming Group/system:masters (the bootstrap binding exempt); client certificates carrying O=system:masters are not visible.


## CIS Kubernetes Benchmark 2.0.1

### Partial

**general**

- `5.6.3` Pods and containers set a securityContext — Root, privilege escalation, privileged, capabilities (added, dangerous, NET_RAW), seccomp, explicit AppArmor Unconfined and readOnlyRootFilesystem are evaluated; runAsGroup and SELinux options are not.

**rbac**

- `5.1.7` No subjects in the system:masters group — Flags RBAC bindings naming Group/system:masters (the bootstrap binding exempt). Membership itself is carried in client certificates: CSRs requesting O=system:masters need a certificates.k8s.io/v1 certificatesigningrequests list (not collected), and certificates minted offline from the CA stay invisible.
